preamble: In Russian akanye unstressed /o/ merges with /a/. In the Moscow standard the merged vowel is the near-open central [ɐ] in the syllable immediately before the stress and in absolute word-initial position, and [ə] in all other unstressed syllables. Yanushevskaya & Bunčić (2015) give [ɐ] as the Moscow and [ʌ] as the St Petersburg realization of this first degree of reduction.

examples.note: Only the first pretonic /o/ is [ɐ]; the second pretonic one is [ə].

languageExamples.context: First pretonic syllable and word-initial position, after hard consonants
